writeup.p: C17 is the plugin-channel transport: a channel String plus a short-length-prefixed byte payload. Vanilla channels cover brand (MC|Brand), books (MC|BEdit, MC|BSign), anvil rename (MC|ItemName), villager trades (MC|TrSel), command blocks (MC|AdvCdm) and channel registration (REGISTER). It is the most structurally open serverbound packet, since the server hands unknown channels to plugin handlers unchanged.

processVanilla250Packet dispatches on channel: MC|BEdit and MC|BSign deserialize an ItemStack and validate its NBT (ItemWritableBook.isNBTValid / ItemEditableBook.validBookTagContents) before applying; MC|TrSel reads an int trade index against the open merchant container; MC|AdvCdm requires command blocks enabled plus permission level 2 and creative mode; MC|ItemName renames the anvil item. Unknown channels are ignored by vanilla. The client side registers MC|Brand once per connection via ClientBrandRetriever.

Five families. (1) Brand spoofing: Rise 5.99 ClientSpoofer rewrites C17 payloads per mode, and the Rise 6.x ClientSpoofer's LabyMod mode cancels and replays six LabyMod/Intave payloads. (2) Disabler payload rewriting: Rise 6.2.4 TestDisabler overwrites every C17 payload with 'eyser'. (3) Console spam: Rise 6.x ChannelConsoleSpammer floods REGISTER. (4) Crash payloads: Rise 5.99 Crasher's BEdit and Mare modes push deeply nested book NBT over MC|BEdit; Tenacity's CrasherCommand floods a fixed C17. (5) Blink: PingSpoofComponent holds C17 in its blink tuple. The two new research clients add two more. LiquidSense Dev filters the channel stream in AntiForge (cancel non-MC| payloads and FMLProxyPacket, rewrite MC|Brand to vanilla), sends a spoofed AntiCheat channel JSON in HYTBypass, floods MC|BSign and MC|BEdit book payloads in ServerCrasher, and forces MC|Brand in MixinNetHandlerPlayClient. November Recode 2.0 has no dedicated C17 module; its LuaEventPacket wrapper maps C17 to id 0x17 for the scripting API.

The brand channel is a fingerprinting surface in both directions: servers read MC|Brand and REGISTER to identify clients, and spoofers forge them. The MC|BEdit path is the crash vector because the server deserializes a full ItemStack and validates deep NBT; the nested {extra:[{...}} page strings in Rise 5.99's BEdit mode are the same family as the C0E and C10 book crashes. REGISTER flooding abuses plugin channel registries that allocate per registration. Behavioral mismatch is the anti-cheat counter: a spoofed brand that behaves unlike the real client is itself a signal.

overview: The plugin-channel packet and the corpus's widest abuse surface: brand spoofing (Rise 5.99 ClientSpoofer, Rise 6.x LabyMod), payload rewriting (TestDisabler), REGISTER flooding (ChannelConsoleSpammer), book-NBT crash payloads (Rise 5.99 Crasher, Tenacity CrasherCommand) and blink-hold integration.
server_handling: processVanilla250Packet: channel dispatch with per-channel validation. MC|BEdit/MC|BSign validate book NBT and throw IOException on invalid tags; MC|AdvCdm gates on command blocks enabled, permission 2 and creative; MC|ItemName renames with a length check; MC|TrSel indexes the open ContainerMerchant. Unknown channels are ignored. The packet data is a PacketBuffer, so parsing is stateful and plugin-dependent.
protocol_notes: String channel + short data length + bytes. The REGISTER channel carries a colon-separated channel list, which is how mods announce handlers. MC|Brand is sent exactly once per connection right after login, which is why brand spoofers tell the user to rejoin. Payloads are length-prefixed shorts, so the 32KB cap applies per payload.
anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats do not parse C17 content; anti-exploit plugins and client-detection plugins do. Client detection reads MC|Brand and REGISTER lists and compares against known client signatures, so spoofing is a cat-and-mouse over payload bytes. Book-NBT crash payloads are detected only by patched parsers. REGISTER flooding is rate-limited by anti-spam plugins.

modules.name: ClientSpoofer
modules.purpose: Rewrite the C17 brand handshake so servers fingerprint the client as Forge, Lunar, LabyMod, PvP Lounge, CheatBreaker or Geyser.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, mutates every C17 in place: sets a new payload (writeString or raw bytes) per mode, and for Lunar also rewrites the channel to REGISTER. Requires a rejoin because MC|Brand is sent once per connection.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: A spoofed brand that behaves unlike the real client (missing plugin channels, wrong packets) is the detectable mismatch; pure payload rewriting is otherwise invisible.
modules.variations: Rise 6.x splits this into a ClientSpoofer module with per-client Modes; LabyMod is the richest of them.

modules.name: LabyMod (client spoofer)
modules.purpose: Fully impersonate the LabyMod handshake: cancel the real C17 and replay six LabyMod and Intave channel payloads.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, cancels the original C17 and sends MC|Brand 'labymod', REGISTER for labymod:neominecraft:intavelabymod3:main, version JSONs on labymod:neo and labymod3:main, and two minecraft:intave clientconfig messages, all via sendNoEvent. The spoofed version defaults to 4.2.31.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The Intave config payloads advertise legacySneakHeight/legacyOldRange/legacyOldSlowdown false, which Intave-based servers read to enable stricter checks; mis-spoofing them can backfire.

modules.name: ChannelConsoleSpammer
modules.purpose: Flood the server with REGISTER payloads naming random MC| channels.
modules.how_it_works: On TickEvent, sends channelsPerTick (1..100) REGISTER packets, each with a random 8-16 letter channel name, via PacketUtil.send.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Detectable by rate limits on REGISTER and by channel-registry memory accounting; it is a console nuisance, not a movement exploit.

modules.name: Crasher (BEdit / Mare)
modules.purpose: Push crafted book NBT over the MC|BEdit channel to crash servers with unpatched book parsers.
modules.how_it_works: Rise 5.99's BEdit mode sends 30 MC|BEdit payloads whose book pages are deeply nested {extra:[{...}} JSON; Mare mode repeats the same construction packets.getValue() times. Tenacity's CrasherCommand floods a fixed C17 with repeated U+1D11E bytes.
modules.vanilla_hook: MotionEvent (Tenacity module path), direct send queue (command path), onPreMotion (Rise 5.99).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The nested-JSON payloads target chat/JSON deserializers; patched servers reject the book NBT via isNBTValid and drop the packet. Rate-based detection is trivial for the 30x flood.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 carries both BEdit and Mare in one Crasher module; Tenacity exposes the flood as a chat command with a configurable packet count.

modules.name: TestDisabler (payload rewrite)
modules.purpose: Rewrite every outgoing C17 payload to fixed bytes as a disabler test mode.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketSendEvent, replaces the C17 buffer with the raw bytes of the string 'eyser' without cancelling the packet.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Corrupting every C17 breaks the brand handshake and any mod channel traffic, which is obvious to client-detection plugins; the mode is experimental by design.
modules.variations: Not present in Rise 6.1.30; Rise 6.1.30's VulcanDisabler carries only a commented-out C17 check.

modules.name: AntiForge (payload filter)
modules.purpose: Strip Forge and mod fingerprints from the C17 stream: cancel non-MC| payloads and FMLProxyPacket, and rewrite MC|Brand to the literal 'vanilla'.
modules.how_it_works: The PacketEvent handler, gated on enabled and not a singleplayer world, cancels FMLProxyPacket by class name, cancels any C17 whose channel does not start with 'MC|', and for MC|Brand replaces the payload with a buffer writing the string 'vanilla'. The file carries an older commented-out handler (lines 28 to 56) that did the same checks in a different order; the live handler merged them.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketEvent (send side), handleEvents returns true so the listener always fires.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Blocking every non-MC| channel breaks mod handshakes, so the client looks vanilla to plugin-channel scanners; the MC|Brand rewrite to 'vanilla' matches what a plain client announces. Servers that fingerprint via REGISTER or modded payloads see a clean stream.
modules.variations: This is the LiquidBounce AntiForge special class shipped inside LiquidSense Dev; November Recode 2.0 has no equivalent module, and its LuaEventPacket only maps C17 to 0x17 for scripts.

modules.name: HYTBypass (AntiCheat payload)
modules.purpose: Send a crafted JSON payload on the 'AntiCheat' channel two seconds after joining a world, advertising a spoofed client fingerprint.
modules.how_it_works: On WorldEvent, spawns a thread that sleeps 2000ms, builds a JsonObject with a base64 hash, the Chinese title for 'Minecraft 1.8.9', isLiquidbounce false, path 'mixins.mcwrapper.json' and the player name, writes it into a PacketBuffer, and sends C17 on channel 'AntiCheat' via the network manager. The payload is aimed at servers whose anti-cheat plugin asks clients to self-identify on that channel.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The payload claims a non-LiquidBounce wrapper (isLiquidbounce false) and a mixin path, a direct counter to servers that fingerprint LiquidSense via the AntiCheat channel; a wrong or missing answer marks the client.
modules.variations: The base64 and mixins.mcwrapper.json fields are specific to this bypass; the module is a one-shot per world join, unlike AntiForge which filters the whole session.

modules.name: ServerCrasher (book flood)
modules.purpose: Crash unpatched servers by flooding MC|BSign and MC|BEdit with book NBT payloads, plus position-spam crash modes in the same module shell.
modules.how_it_works: BookFlood mode, on every pre-motion tick, builds an ItemStack writable book with a 50-page NBTTagList of 600-character random strings and sends 100 C17 payloads alternating MC|BSign and MC|BEdit, each writing the book ItemStack into a fresh PacketBuffer. The other modes are position based (AACNew and AACOther flood C04 at huge offsets, MassiveChunkLoading steps y to 255) or chat based (WorldEdit //calc, Pex /pex promote).
modules.vanilla_hook: onEnable (one-shot modes), MotionEvent PRE (BookFlood loop), WorldEvent and TickEvent (self-disable guards).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The 100-per-tick book flood is the same family as Rise 5.99's Crasher BEdit and Tenacity's CrasherCommand: deep NBT deserialization on the server. The random channel choice between BSign and BEdit doubles the parser paths hit.
modules.variations: The channel alternation and 50-page by 600-char page construction differ from Rise's nested JSON pages; the module is the only crash tool in the two new clients.

modules.name: LuaEventPacket (scripting wrapper)
modules.purpose: Expose C17 (and every other serverbound class) to Lua scripts as a numeric packet id plus direction.
modules.how_it_works: A static map binds each packet class to its protocol id, C17 at 0x17; the LuaEventPacket constructor resolves the incoming EventPacket's class through the map and records 'out' for EventPacket.Out sends, 'in' otherwise. The @DontObfuscate annotation keeps the class name readable so the Lua runtime can reflect it.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket wrap point in the scripting engine.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: This is a scripting surface, not an exploit: it lets user scripts intercept and rewrite C17 traffic; the map is the ground truth the Lua API uses instead of reflection, because obfuscation would break class lookups.
modules.variations: The same wrapper backs every packet impl in this corpus; November Recode 2.0 has no dedicated C17 module, so this map entry is its only corpus appearance for C17.

general_hooks: PacketSendEvent for rewrite/cancel (Rise 5.99, Rise 6.x), TickEvent for REGISTER floods, direct send-queue pushes for crash commands (Tenacity).
client_variations: Rise 5.99 mutates the packet in place; Rise 6.x cancels and replays via sendNoEvent; Tenacity pushes raw packets into the vanilla send queue. PingSpoofComponent additionally holds C17 in its blink tuple in both Rise 6.x builds. LiquidSense Dev filters and rewrites C17 in its PacketEvent (AntiForge), sends crafted payloads on world join (HYTBypass), floods book channels (ServerCrasher), and forces MC|Brand in MixinNetHandlerPlayClient. November Recode 2.0 exposes C17 to Lua scripts via LuaEventPacket (id 0x17). LiquidSense's MemoryFixer imports C17PacketCustomPayload but never uses it; the import is dead code and the module only calls System.gc on a timer.
